title: Mid-week Rapid Rollout Decision Journal
content:
Meeting: Mid-week Rapid Rollout planning & emergency hotpatch triage
Date: 2025-02-12 (standup at 10:00 PT)
Owners: Diego Morales (release lead), Aisha Patel (SRE on-call), Rebecca Chen (runtime eng), Omar Singh (QA lead)
Attendees: list above + on-call rotation (Elena on standby)
Purpose: decide whether to proceed with accelerated rollout of runtime patch v1.14.3 to hosted clusters, and capture manual mitigation knobs & rollback criteria in case of regression. This doc records the decisions, owner lattice, open questions, and action items for follow-up.

Summary/Status snapshot
- Trigger: customer-reported tokenization mismatch on long-context (>16k) prompts (customer: AcmeTranslate). Repro rate ~0.25% on long tails, failsafe for shorter contexts unaffected.
- Patch: runtime: fix for streaming KV cache boundary condition + improved error logging. Patch is built and smoke-tested on staging (runtime/nightly->v1.14.3).
- Risk posture: medium — bug affects long sequence corner cases; rolling to all hosts could expose production traffic; canary expected to catch regressions but timing is tight due to upcoming demo on Tue 02/18.

Decisions made
1) Proceed with rapid rollout in three phases starting 02/13: small canary (5% traffic), monitored for 60m; expanded canary (25%) for 3h if no new anomalies; ramp to 100% over 24h only if aggregated error delta <0.05% and latency P95 delta <10ms.
2) Enable conservative surge-capacity knobs during canary: cap batch size to 8 for canary replicas and enforce KV cache TTL=30s to minimize cross-request coupling.
3) Activate emergency fallback route to model-variant (gpt-medium-optimized) for affected routes if error rate crosses 0.5% absolute increase vs baseline in 15m window.
4) Owner lattice: release lead -> Diego Morales; canary ops -> Aisha Patel; rollback authority -> SRE manager (Elena Karpov); QA signoff -> Omar Singh; runtime owner -> Rebecca Chen. Each owner must acknowledge via Slack before next phase.

Monitoring & SLOs to watch (who monitors)
- Request error rate (4xx/5xx) — primary signal (Aisha)
- Model output divergence metrics (eval harness on sample prompts) — QA (Omar)
- Latency P50/P95/P99 token generation for long contexts — runtime (Rebecca)
- Resource saturation (GPU mem, CPU steal) & scaling events — infra (SRE)
- Cost delta estimate (per-token cost) during burst — Diego
Thresholds that trigger automated mitigation
- >=0.5% absolute error-rate increase over baseline within 15m -> auto-fallback to variant + alert to owner lattice
- Latency P95 increase >10ms sustained for 30m -> pause ramp and investigate
- Any memory OOMs or KV cache corruptions -> immediate rollback to previous runtime build

Rollout checklist (pre-canary)
- [x] Bake container image and publish digest (runtime:v1.14.3) (Rebecca)
- [x] Run smoke tests on staging with 100 random long-context traces (Omar)
- [x] Create canary traffic slice and routing policy (policy id: canary-2025-02-13-1) (Diego)
- [x] Prepare QuickPlay eval set (50 prompts from AcmeTranslate corpus, anonymized) (QA)
- [ ] Add temporary tracing hooks for KV boundary logging (Rebecca) — TODO before canary expansion
- [ ] Notify customer success & account team for AcmeTranslate (Diego)

Open questions / ambiguities
- Does the billing meter for reduced batch size during canary need a temporary exception for cost reconciliation? (finance ops)
- How will Dedicated customers on pinned clusters be notified/handled if they consume the same runtime build? (product-private)
- If the canary shows slight increases in nonfunctional divergence (e.g., tokenization subtle shifts) below alert thresholds, do we require formal model-eval approval before wider ramp? Decision: treat as 'yellow' and require QA signoff to proceed.

Hotfix edgecases observed in staging (notes)
- Intermittent KV eviction caused by corner sequence where consecutive prefix flush triggered a stale pointer — reproduced 3/1000 in stress harness. Fixed by pointer null-check + metrics.
- Logging: previous logs aggregated multiple snippets; added structured event id for easier cross-correlation (trace_id + kv_seq).

Communication plan
- Slack: #release-ops pinned message at start of canary with links to dashboard and playbook; owner pings required when promoting phase.
- Email: short note to account team and CS for customers with >1% long-context usage.
- Postmortem: if rollback occurs, do a 48h blameless postmortem with timeline, root cause, and regression gate analysis.

Action items (owners + ETA)
- Rebecca: push tracing hook & re-run smoke tests with hooks enabled (ETA: 02/12 18:00 PT)
- Aisha: prepare monitoring dashboard and automated PagerDuty escalation (ETA: 02/13 08:00 PT)
- Omar: baseline evaluation run and snapshot diffs for quick QA signoff (ETA: 02/13 09:00 PT)
- Diego: notify CS/AMs and schedule 30m decision call at end of small canary window (ETA: before 02/13 12:30 PT)
- Elena: confirm rollback playbook and ensure SRE manager available during canary window (ETA: 02/13 09:30 PT)

Quick retrospective notes (post-standup thoughts)
- Consider adding a lightweight chaos test to nightly to flush KV pointers earlier in CI so we catch similar regressions sooner.
- We should formalize a "minor runtime patch" decision matrix (thresholds, owner matrix) to reduce meeting overhead for future small-risk patches.

Notes to self (informal scribbles)
- If canary shows false-positive noise, lower sample window to 5m for automated alerts but require human confirmation before rollback.
- Double-check Dedicated customers' upgrade policy — may need opt-in toggle.

References & tickets
- RELEASE-842: production tokenization mismatch (link above)
- OPS-3095: canary rollout policy template
- GH PR: runtime/pull/1427 (fix + new logging)

Next sync: rapid-rollout decision call 02/13 12:30 PT (15 min) — owners only

-- end of journal entry --
_notes: informal: draft used for synchronous decision making; to be converted into formal rollout playbook if we proceed
